# fb_parse FILE GATE → one compact JSON object: {file, exists, trailer, verdict,
# counts, exit_code, sprint_id, ts, approved, hash}. The hash is the run-mode
# same-issue hash (md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` over verdict-derive's
# --json output; legacy files hash their findings section).
fb_parse() {
  local f="$1" g="$2" rel vj tl pj hash
  rel="${f#"$root"/}"
  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then jq -nc --arg f "$rel" '{file: $f, exists: false}'; return 0; fi
  vj=$(bash "$VERDICT_DERIVE" --file "$f" --gate "$g" --json 2>/dev/null) || true
  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$vj" || vj='{"trailer_found":false,"verdict":null,"counts":null,"exit_code":1}'
  tl=$(grep -E '^<!-- LOA-VERDICT \{.*\} -->[[:space:]]*$' "$f" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1) || tl=""
  pj=$(printf '%s' "$tl" | sed -E 's/^<!-- LOA-VERDICT (.*) -->[[:space:]]*$/\1/')
  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'
  if [[ "$(jq -r '.trailer_found' <<<"$vj")" == true ]]; then
    hash=$(printf '%s\n' "$vj" | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
  else
    hash=$( { grep -A 100 "## Findings\|## Issues\|## Changes Required" "$f" 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -50 | _md5)
  fi
  jq -nc --arg f "$rel" --argjson v "$vj" --argjson p "$pj" --arg h "$hash" '
    def sid: if type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$") then . else null end;
    def tsv: if type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$") then . else null end;
    {file: $f, exists: true, trailer: ($v.trailer_found == true),
     verdict: ($v.verdict | if type == "string" then . else null end),
     counts: ($v.counts // null), exit_code: ($v.exit_code // 1),
     sprint_id: ($p.sprint_id | sid), ts: ($p.ts | tsv), hash: $h}
    | .approved = (.exit_code == 0 and .verdict == "APPROVED")'
}

# impl_commit SINCE → "sha epoch" of the newest non-merge commit on HEAD since
# SINCE touching a path outside the state/generated set, or nothing
impl_commit() {
  git -C "$root" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  git -C "$root" log --no-merges -n 1 --format='%H %ct' ${1:+"--since=$1"} -- . \
    ':(exclude,glob)grimoires/**' ':(exclude,glob).run/**' ':(exclude,glob)**/REPO-MAP.md' \
    ':(exclude,glob)**/checksums.json' ':(exclude,glob)**/CHANGELOG.md' 2>/dev/null || true
}

# The ordered rounds of one sprint directory: every -rN file, then the current
# file unless it is byte-identical to the highest -rN of its gate
rounds_of() {
  local dir="$1" g base f n top topn cur
  for g in review audit; do
    if [[ "$g" == review ]]; then base=engineer-feedback; else base=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
    top=""; topn=-1
    for f in "$dir/$base"-r*.md; do
      [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
      n=${f##*-r}; n=${n%.md}
      [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]{1,6}$ ]] || continue
      fb_parse "$f" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" --argjson n "$((10#$n))" '. + {gate: $g, round: $n}'
      if (( 10#$n > topn )); then topn=$((10#$n)); top="$f"; fi
    done
    cur="$dir/$base.md"
    if [[ -f "$cur" ]] && ! { [[ -n "$top" ]] && cmp -s "$cur" "$top"; }; then
      fb_parse "$cur" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" '. + {gate: $g, round: 999999}'
    fi
  done
}

# Shared jq definitions: time, the breaker recompute and the run-state resolution
JQ_DEFS='
def epoch: if type == "string" then (sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) else null end;
def fresh($now; $win): epoch as $t | $t != null and ($now - $t) <= $win and ($t - $now) <= 300;
def recompute($rounds; $reset):
  ($rounds
   | map(select($reset == null or ((.ts // "") > $reset)))
   | sort_by([(.ts // ""), .round, (if .gate == "review" then 0 else 1 end)])
   | map(select(.approved | not))) as $nr
  | reduce $nr[] as $r ({cycle: 0, same: 0, hash: null, np: 0, lc: null};
      .cycle += 1
      | (if $r.hash != "none" and $r.hash == .hash then .same += 1 else .same = 1 | .hash = $r.hash end)
      | ($r.counts | tojson) as $c
      | (if .lc != null and .lc == $c then .np += 1 else .np = 0 end)
      | .lc = $c);
def skeleton($th; $ts):
  {state: "CLOSED",
   triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: $th.same, last_hash: null},
              no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: $th.np},
              cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: $th.cycles},
              timeout: {started: $ts, limit_hours: $th.hours}},
   history: []};
def merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts):
  (if type == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
  | .triggers = (.triggers // {})
  | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ([(.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0), $rc.cycle] | max)
  | (if $rc.same > (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0)
     then .triggers.same_issue.count = $rc.same | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $rc.hash else . end)
  | (if $rc.np > (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) or (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts == null and $rc.lc != null)
     then .triggers.no_progress.count = ([(.triggers.no_progress.count // 0), $rc.np] | max)
          | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $rc.lc else . end)
  | ( if (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
        then ["same_issue", "same issue hash repeated \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times (derived from the feedback history)"]
      elif (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
        then ["no_progress", "counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
      elif (.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
        then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
      else null end ) as $trip
  | if $trip != null and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
    then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], source: "derive"}])
    else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end;
def known_ids: (.derivation.sprint_ids // null) // ((.sprints.list // []) | map(.id? // empty));
def resolve($f; $now; $win):
  . as $c
  | (if ($c | type) == "object" then $c else {} end) as $c
  | ($c.state // $c.status // "") as $cs
  | ($c | known_ids) as $known
  | ([$f.sprints[] | select(.state != "complete")
      | "sprint-\(.global_id)" as $g | .local_label as $l
      | select(($known | index($g)) == null and ($l == "" or ($known | index($l)) == null))] | length > 0) as $new
  | ((($c.completion // {}) | .merged_sha? // "") | type == "string" and length > 0) as $merged
  | if ($c.state // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or ($c.status // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or $merged then "JACKED_OUT"
    elif $f.breaker_open or $cs == "HALTED" then "HALTED"
    elif $f.all_complete then "COMPLETE"
    elif $cs == "COMPLETE" and ($new | not) then "COMPLETE"
    elif ($c.timestamps.last_activity? // null) | fresh($now; $win) then "RUNNING"
    else "INTERRUPTED" end;
'

cmd_derive() {
  local ledger="$root/grimoires/loa/ledger.json" a2a="$root/grimoires/loa/a2a" active rows
  if [[ ! -f "$ledger" ]] || ! jq -e 'type == "object"' "$ledger" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "run-checkpoint: derive: no readable ledger at $ledger — callers keep the cache" >&2; return 4
  fi
  active=$(jq -r '.active_cycle // empty | strings' "$ledger")
  if [[ -z "$active" ]] || ! jq -e --arg c "$active" 'any(.cycles[]?; .id == $c)' "$ledger" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "run-checkpoint: derive: the ledger has no active cycle — callers keep the cache" >&2; return 4
  fi
  local win now now_ts fa=1 th
  win=$(( $(cfg_int '.run_mode.stale_hours' 12 8760) * 3600 ))
  [[ "$(cfg '.run_mode.file_authoritative')" == false ]] && fa=0
  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
  now=$(date +%s); now_ts=$(now_iso)

  # Per-sprint facts
  local sprints="[]" gid label lstatus since dir rv au mex msid ic sj
  rows=$(jq -r --arg c "$active" '
    (.cycles[] | select(.id == $c)) as $cy
    | ($cy.sprints // [])[]
    | select((.global_id | type) == "number")
    | [(.global_id | tostring), ((.local_label // "") | tostring), ((.status // "") | tostring),
       ([.started, .created, $cy.created] | map(select(type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-")))
        | if length == 0 then "" else ([.[0], ($cy.created // "")] | max) end)]
    | map(if . == "" then "-" else . end)
    | @tsv' "$ledger")
  # "-" stands for an empty field: IFS whitespace (tab) would collapse two adjacent separators
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r gid label lstatus since; do
    [[ "$gid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
    [[ "$label" == - ]] && label=""
    [[ "$since" == - ]] && since=""
    [[ "$label" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$ ]] || label=""
    [[ "$lstatus" =~ ^[a-z_]{1,32}$ ]] || lstatus="unknown"
    [[ "$since" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$ ]] || since=""
    dir="$a2a/sprint-$gid"
    rv=$(fb_parse "$dir/engineer-feedback.md" review)
    au=$(fb_parse "$dir/auditor-sprint-feedback.md" audit)
    mex=false; msid=""
    if [[ -f "$dir/COMPLETED" ]]; then
      mex=true
      msid=$(sed -n 's/^sprint:[[:space:]]*\([A-Za-z0-9._-]*\).*/\1/p' "$dir/COMPLETED" | head -n 1) || msid=""
    fi
    ic=$(impl_commit "$since")
    sj=$(jq -nc --argjson gid "$gid" --arg label "$label" --arg status "$lstatus" --argjson rv "$rv" --argjson au "$au" \
              --argjson mex "$mex" --arg msid "$msid" --arg ic "$ic" '
      def mine: type == "string" and length > 0 and (. == "sprint-\($gid)" or ($label != "" and . == $label));
      ($rv.approved == true and ($rv.sprint_id | mine)) as $R
      | ($au.approved == true and ($au.sprint_id | mine)) as $A
      | ([$rv.sprint_id, $au.sprint_id, (if $msid == "" then null else $msid end)] | map(select(type == "string" and length > 0))) as $ids
      | ($mex and any($ids[]; mine | not)) as $stale
      | ($mex and ($stale | not) and (($rv.sprint_id | mine) or ($au.sprint_id | mine))) as $M
      | ($ic | split(" ")) as $c
      | ([$rv.ts, $au.ts] | map(select(. != null)) | max) as $vts
      | def verdict($x): if $x.exists then {verdict: $x.verdict, sprint_id: $x.sprint_id, consistent: ($x.exit_code == 0), file: $x.file} else null end;
      {global_id: $gid, local_label: $label, status: $status,
       completed_marker: $M, marker_present: $mex, stale_marker: $stale,
       review: verdict($rv), audit: verdict($au),
       impl_commit: (if ($c | length) == 2 then $c[0] else null end),
       commit_after_verdict: (if ($c | length) == 2 and $vts != null
                              then (($c[1] | tonumber) > ($vts | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch 0)) else null end),
       legacy_feedback: ([$rv, $au] | map(select(.exists and (.trailer | not)) | .file)),
       state: (if $M and $R and $A and $status == "completed" then "complete"
               elif ($M | not) and $R and $A then "awaiting_marker" else "in_progress" end)}')
    sprints=$(jq -c --argjson s "$sj" '. + [$s]' <<<"$sprints")
  done <<<"$rows"

  # Breaker recompute over the active sprint's ordered rounds
  local active_gid rounds cache="null" cache_ok=1 bcache="null" reset rc merged
  active_gid=$(jq -r 'if length == 0 then "" else ((map(select(.state != "complete")) | .[0]) // .[-1]) | .global_id | tostring end' <<<"$sprints")
  rounds="[]"
  if [[ -n "$active_gid" && -d "$a2a/sprint-$active_gid" ]]; then
    rounds=$(rounds_of "$a2a/sprint-$active_gid" | jq -sc '.')
  fi
  if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
    if cache=$(jq -c . "$file" 2>/dev/null) && [[ -n "$cache" ]]; then :; else cache="null"; cache_ok=0; fi
  fi
  if [[ -f "$breaker" ]]; then bcache=$(jq -c 'if type == "object" then . else null end' "$breaker" 2>/dev/null) || bcache="null"; [[ -n "$bcache" ]] || bcache="null"; fi
  reset=$(jq -c '.reset_at? // null | if type == "string" then . else null end' <<<"$bcache")
  rc=$(jq -nc --argjson r "$rounds" --argjson z "$reset" "$JQ_DEFS"' recompute($r; $z)')
  merged=$(jq -c --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' <<<"$bcache")

  local facts report
  facts=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$sprints" --argjson b "$merged" '
    {sprints: $s,
     all_complete: (($s | length) > 0 and all($s[]; .state == "complete")),
     breaker_open: ($b.state == "OPEN"),
     stale_markers: [$s[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id)"],
     legacy_feedback: [$s[] | .legacy_feedback[]],
     sprint_ids: [$s[] | "sprint-\(.global_id)"]}')
  report=$(jq -nc --argjson f "$facts" --argjson c "$cache" --argjson b "$merged" --argjson rc "$rc" \
                  --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" --arg cycle "$active" \
                  --argjson fa "$fa" --argjson cache_ok "$cache_ok" --arg ag "$active_gid" "$JQ_DEFS"'
    def st: if type == "string" then (if test("^[A-Z_]{1,32}$") then . else "INVALID" end) else null end;
    ($c | resolve($f; $now; $win)) as $s
    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.state | st) else null end) as $cs
    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.status | st) else null end) as $cst
    | {cycle: $cycle, derived_at: $ts, stale_hours: ($win / 3600), file_authoritative: ($fa == 1),
       state: $s, cache_state: $cs, cache_status: $cst,
       cache: (if $cache_ok == 0 then "unparseable" elif $c == null then "missing" else "present" end),
       drift: ($c != null and ($cs != $s or ($cst != null and $cst != $s))),
       notes: ([
         (if $cs != null and $cst != null and $cs != $cst then "cache .state \($cs) and .status \($cst) disagree" else empty end),
         (if $s == "JACKED_OUT" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "JACKED_OUT is terminal: files show incomplete sprints; the cache is kept" else empty end),
         (if $s == "COMPLETE" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "COMPLETE kept: no new incomplete sprint in the ledger" else empty end),
         ($f.sprints[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id): COMPLETED marker names another sprint (stale_marker, not counted)"),
         ($f.sprints[] | select(.state == "awaiting_marker") | "sprint-\(.global_id): review and audit APPROVED, no COMPLETED marker")
       ]),
       sprints: $f.sprints,
       active_sprint: (if $ag == "" then null else "sprint-\($ag)" end),
       breaker: {state: $b.state, cycle_count: $b.triggers.cycle_count.current, same_issue: $b.triggers.same_issue.count,
                 no_progress: $b.triggers.no_progress.count, recomputed: {cycle_count: $rc.cycle, same_issue: $rc.same, no_progress: $rc.np}},
       derivation: {source: "files", stale_markers: $f.stale_markers, legacy_feedback: $f.legacy_feedback},
       written: false}')

  if (( write )); then
    local why=""
    if (( fa == 0 )); then why="run_mode.file_authoritative: false — report-only"
    elif [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then why="no run state at $file — nothing to rewrite"
    elif (( cache_ok == 0 )); then why="$file unparseable — kept for inspection, not rewritten"
    fi
    if [[ -z "$why" ]]; then
      atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' || return 3
      merged=$(jq -c . "$breaker")
      facts=$(jq -c --argjson b "$merged" '.breaker_open = ($b.state == "OPEN")' <<<"$facts")
      atomic_update "$file" --argjson f "$facts" --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"'
        resolve($f; $now; $win) as $s
        | .state = $s | .status = $s | .derived_at = $ts
        | .derivation = {source: "files", stale_markers: $f.stale_markers, legacy_feedback: $f.legacy_feedback, sprint_ids: $f.sprint_ids}
        | .schema_version = (.schema_version // 2)' || return 3
      report=$(jq -c --slurpfile c "$file" --argjson b "$merged" '.written = true | .state = $c[0].state | .breaker.state = $b.state' <<<"$report")
    else
      report=$(jq -c --arg w "$why" '.notes += [$w]' <<<"$report")
    fi
  fi

  if (( json )); then
    jq . <<<"$report"
  else
    jq -r '"derive: files say \(.state), cache said \(.cache_state // "nothing") (\(if .drift then "drift" else "in sync" end))"
           + (if .written then " — caches rewritten" else "" end), (.notes[] | "  note: " + .)' <<<"$report"
  fi
  return 0
}

cmd_record_round() {
  [[ -n "$gate" && -n "$file" ]] || usage
  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: record-round: no feedback file at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
  local p th ts now out trip
  p=$(fb_parse "$file" "$gate")
  if [[ "$(jq -r '.approved' <<<"$p")" == true ]]; then
    echo "recorded: $gate APPROVED — breaker counters unchanged"
    return 0
  fi
  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
  ts=$(now_iso); now=$(date +%s)
  atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson p "$p" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$ts" --argjson now "$now" \
      --arg gate "$gate" --arg sprint "$sprint" "$JQ_DEFS"'
    (if type == "object" and (.triggers | type) == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
    | ($p.counts | tojson) as $c
    | (if $p.hash != "none" and $p.hash == (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash // null)
       then .triggers.same_issue.count = ((.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) + 1)
       else .triggers.same_issue.count = 1 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $p.hash end)
    | (if (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts // null) != null and .triggers.no_progress.last_counts == $c
       then .triggers.no_progress.count = ((.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) + 1)
       else .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 end)
    | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $c
    | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ((.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) + 1)
    | (.triggers.timeout.started // null | epoch) as $start
    | ( if .triggers.same_issue.count >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
          then ["same_issue", "same issue hash \($p.hash[0:8]) seen \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times in a row"]
        elif .triggers.no_progress.count >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
          then ["no_progress", "finding counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds"]
        elif .triggers.cycle_count.current >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
          then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds reached the limit \(.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)"]
        elif $start != null and ($now - $start) >= ((.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) * 3600)
          then ["timeout", "run older than \(.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) hours"]
        elif (.state // "CLOSED") == "OPEN" then ["open", "breaker already OPEN"]
        else null end ) as $trip
    | .last_round = {gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end), verdict: $p.verdict, hash: $p.hash, ts: $ts}
    | if $trip != null and $trip[0] != "open" and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
      then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end)}])
      elif $trip != null then .state = "OPEN"

tool_use_result.stdout:
# A task checkpoint is trusted only when beads CONFIRMS the task closed;
    # "br unavailable" is not a confirmation (Bridgebuilder PR #1269 FIND-003).
    brc=0; bead_closed "$t" || brc=$?
    case $brc in 0) ;; 2) reason="beads unavailable — task $t cannot be verified";; *) reason="task $t is not closed in beads";; esac
  fi
  if [[ -n "$reason" ]]; then
    echo "run-checkpoint: discarding checkpoint ($reason) — resume from the first open bead of $s" >&2
    if (( json )); then jq -cn --arg r "$reason" --arg s "$s" '{checkpoint:null, reason:$r, sprint:$s}'; else echo "checkpoint: discarded ($reason); resume at the first open bead of $s"; fi
    return 0
  fi
  if (( json )); then jq -c '{checkpoint: .checkpoint}' "$file"
  else echo "checkpoint: $s ${t:+task $t }phase $p at $ts → resume at the first open bead after $t in $s"; fi
}

# fb_parse FILE GATE → one compact JSON object: {file, exists, trailer, verdict,
# counts, exit_code, sprint_id, ts, approved, hash}. The hash is the run-mode
# same-issue hash (md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` over verdict-derive's
# --json output; legacy files hash their findings section).
fb_parse() {
  local f="$1" g="$2" rel vj tl pj hash
  rel="${f#"$root"/}"
  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then jq -nc --arg f "$rel" '{file: $f, exists: false}'; return 0; fi
  vj=$(bash "$VERDICT_DERIVE" --file "$f" --gate "$g" --json 2>/dev/null) || true
  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$vj" || vj='{"trailer_found":false,"verdict":null,"counts":null,"exit_code":1}'
  tl=$(grep -E '^<!-- LOA-VERDICT \{.*\} -->[[:space:]]*$' "$f" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1) || tl=""
  pj=$(printf '%s' "$tl" | sed -E 's/^<!-- LOA-VERDICT (.*) -->[[:space:]]*$/\1/')
  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'
  if [[ "$(jq -r '.trailer_found' <<<"$vj")" == true ]]; then
    hash=$(printf '%s\n' "$vj" | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
  else
    hash=$( { grep -A 100 "## Findings\|## Issues\|## Changes Required" "$f" 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -50 | _md5)
  fi
  jq -nc --arg f "$rel" --argjson v "$vj" --argjson p "$pj" --arg h "$hash" '
    def sid: if type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$") then . else null end;
    def tsv: if type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$") then . else null end;
    {file: $f, exists: true, trailer: ($v.trailer_found == true),
     verdict: ($v.verdict | if type == "string" then . else null end),
     counts: ($v.counts // null), exit_code: ($v.exit_code // 1),
     sprint_id: ($p.sprint_id | sid), ts: ($p.ts | tsv), hash: $h}
    | .approved = (.exit_code == 0 and .verdict == "APPROVED")'
}

# impl_commit SINCE → "sha epoch" of the newest non-merge commit on HEAD since
# SINCE touching a path outside the state/generated set, or nothing
impl_commit() {
  git -C "$root" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  git -C "$root" log --no-merges -n 1 --format='%H %ct' ${1:+"--since=$1"} -- . \
    ':(exclude,glob)grimoires/**' ':(exclude,glob).run/**' ':(exclude,glob)**/REPO-MAP.md' \
    ':(exclude,glob)**/checksums.json' ':(exclude,glob)**/CHANGELOG.md' 2>/dev/null || true
}

# The ordered rounds of one sprint directory: every -rN file, then the current
# file unless it is byte-identical to the highest -rN of its gate
rounds_of() {
  local dir="$1" g base f n top topn cur
  for g in review audit; do
    if [[ "$g" == review ]]; then base=engineer-feedback; else base=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
    top=""; topn=-1
    for f in "$dir/$base"-r*.md; do
      [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
      n=${f##*-r}; n=${n%.md}
      [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]{1,6}$ ]] || continue
      fb_parse "$f" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" --argjson n "$((10#$n))" '. + {gate: $g, round: $n}'
      if (( 10#$n > topn )); then topn=$((10#$n)); top="$f"; fi
    done
    cur="$dir/$base.md"
    if [[ -f "$cur" ]] && ! { [[ -n "$top" ]] && cmp -s "$cur" "$top"; }; then
      fb_parse "$cur" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" '. + {gate: $g, round: 999999}'
    fi
  done
}

# Shared jq definitions: time, the breaker recompute and the run-state resolution
JQ_DEFS='
def epoch: if type == "string" then (sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) else null end;
def fresh($now; $win): epoch as $t | $t != null and ($now - $t) <= $win and ($t - $now) <= 300;
def recompute($rounds; $reset):
  ($rounds
   | map(select($reset == null or ((.ts // "") > $reset)))
   | sort_by([(.ts // ""), .round, (if .gate == "review" then 0 else 1 end)])
   | map(select(.approved | not))) as $nr
  | reduce $nr[] as $r ({cycle: 0, same: 0, hash: null, np: 0, lc: null};
      .cycle += 1
      | (if $r.hash != "none" and $r.hash == .hash then .same += 1 else .same = 1 | .hash = $r.hash end)
      | ($r.counts | tojson) as $c
      | (if .lc != null and .lc == $c then .np += 1 else .np = 0 end)
      | .lc = $c);
def skeleton($th; $ts):
  {state: "CLOSED",
   triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: $th.same, last_hash: null},
              no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: $th.np},
              cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: $th.cycles},
              timeout: {started: $ts, limit_hours: $th.hours}},
   history: []};
def merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts):
  (if type == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
  | .triggers = (.triggers // {})
  | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ([(.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0), $rc.cycle] | max)
  | (if $rc.same > (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0)
     then .triggers.same_issue.count = $rc.same | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $rc.hash else . end)
  | (if $rc.np > (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) or (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts == null and $rc.lc != null)
     then .triggers.no_progress.count = ([(.triggers.no_progress.count // 0), $rc.np] | max)
          | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $rc.lc else . end)
  | ( if (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
        then ["same_issue", "same issue hash repeated \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times (derived from the feedback history)"]
      elif (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
        then ["no_progress", "counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
      elif (.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
        then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
      else null end ) as $trip
  | if $trip != null and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
    then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], source: "derive"}])
    else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end;
def known_ids: (.derivation.sprint_ids // null) // ((.sprints.list // []) | map(.id? // empty));
def resolve($f; $now; $win):
  . as $c
  | (if ($c | type) == "object" then $c else {} end) as $c
  | ($c.state // $c.status // "") as $cs
  | ($c | known_ids) as $known
  | ([$f.sprints[] | select(.state != "complete")
      | "sprint-\(.global_id)" as $g | .local_label as $l
      | select(($known | index($g)) == null and ($l == "" or ($known | index($l)) == null))] | length > 0) as $new
  | ((($c.completion // {}) | .merged_sha? // "") | type == "string" and length > 0) as $merged
  | if ($c.state // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or ($c.status // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or $merged then "JACKED_OUT"
    elif $f.breaker_open or $cs == "HALTED" then "HALTED"
    elif $f.all_complete then "COMPLETE"
    elif $cs == "COMPLETE" and ($new | not) then "COMPLETE"
    elif ($c.timestamps.last_activity? // null) | fresh($now; $win) then "RUNNING"
    else "INTERRUPTED" end;
'

cmd_derive() {
  local ledger="$root/grimoires/loa/ledger.json" a2a="$root/grimoires/loa/a2a" active rows
  if [[ ! -f "$ledger" ]] || ! jq -e 'type == "object"' "$ledger" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "run-checkpoint: derive: no readable ledger at $ledger — callers keep the cache" >&2; return 4
  fi
  active=$(jq -r '.active_cycle // empty | strings' "$ledger")
  if [[ -z "$active" ]] || ! jq -e --arg c "$active" 'any(.cycles[]?; .id == $c)' "$ledger" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "run-checkpoint: derive: the ledger has no active cycle — callers keep the cache" >&2; return 4
  fi
  local win now now_ts fa=1 th
  win=$(( $(cfg_int '.run_mode.stale_hours' 12 8760) * 3600 ))
  [[ "$(cfg '.run_mode.file_authoritative')" == false ]] && fa=0
  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
  now=$(date +%s); now_ts=$(now_iso)

  # Per-sprint facts
  local sprints="[]" gid label lstatus since dir rv au mex msid ic sj
  rows=$(jq -r --arg c "$active" '
    (.cycles[] | select(.id == $c)) as $cy
    | ($cy.sprints // [])[]
    | select((.global_id | type) == "number")
    | [(.global_id | tostring), ((.local_label // "") | tostring), ((.status // "") | tostring),
       ([.started, .created, $cy.created] | map(select(type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-")))
        | if length == 0 then "" else ([.[0], ($cy.created // "")] | max) end)]
    | map(if . == "" then "-" else . end)
    | @tsv' "$ledger")
  # "-" stands for an empty field: IFS whitespace (tab) would collapse two adjacent separators
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r gid label lstatus since; do
    [[ "$gid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
    [[ "$label" == - ]] && label=""
    [[ "$since" == - ]] && since=""
    [[ "$label" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$ ]] || label=""
    [[ "$lstatus" =~ ^[a-z_]{1,32}$ ]] || lstatus="unknown"
    [[ "$since" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$ ]] || since=""
    dir="$a2a/sprint-$gid"
    rv=$(fb_parse "$dir/engineer-feedback.md" review)
    au=$(fb_parse "$dir/auditor-sprint-feedback.md" audit)
    mex=false; msid=""
    if [[ -f "$dir/COMPLETED" ]]; then
      mex=true
      msid=$(sed -n 's/^sprint:[[:space:]]*\([A-Za-z0-9._-]*\).*/\1/p' "$dir/COMPLETED" | head -n 1) || msid=""
    fi
    ic=$(impl_commit "$since")
    sj=$(jq -nc --argjson gid "$gid" --arg label "$label" --arg status "$lstatus" --argjson rv "$rv" --argjson au "$au" \

cmd_read() {
  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
  if ! jq -e . "$file" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "run-checkpoint: $file unparseable — no checkpoint; beads are the recovery truth" >&2; if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"unparseable"}'; fi; return 0; fi
  local sv cp s t p ts reason="" brc
  sv=$(jq -r '.schema_version // 1' "$file"); cp=$(jq -c '.checkpoint // null' "$file")
  [[ "$sv" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || sv=1
  if [[ "$cp" == "null" || "$sv" -lt 2 ]]; then
    if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"sprint granularity"}'; else echo "checkpoint: none (schema_version $sv → sprint granularity; resume at the first open bead of sprints.current)"; fi
    return 0
  fi
  s=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.sprint // empty' "$file"); t=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.task // empty' "$file"); p=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.phase // empty' "$file"); ts=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.ts // empty' "$file")
  if [[ -z "$s" || -z "$p" ]]; then reason="malformed checkpoint"
  elif [[ -n "$t" ]]; then
    # A task checkpoint is trusted only when beads CONFIRMS the task closed;
    # "br unavailable" is not a confirmation (Bridgebuilder PR #1269 FIND-003).
    brc=0; bead_closed "$t" || brc=$?
    case $brc in 0) ;; 2) reason="beads unavailable — task $t cannot be verified";; *) reason="task $t is not closed in beads";; esac
  fi
  if [[ -n "$reason" ]]; then
    echo "run-checkpoint: discarding checkpoint ($reason) — resume from the first open bead of $s" >&2
    if (( json )); then jq -cn --arg r "$reason" --arg s "$s" '{checkpoint:null, reason:$r, sprint:$s}'; else echo "checkpoint: discarded ($reason); resume at the first open bead of $s"; fi
    return 0
  fi
  if (( json )); then jq -c '{checkpoint: .checkpoint}' "$file"
  else echo "checkpoint: $s ${t:+task $t }phase $p at $ts → resume at the first open bead after $t in $s"; fi
}

+# Prints the heading of an optional table section; returns 1 when the section

+optional_table_heading() {
+  local section="$1" entry o_name o_heading
+  for entry in "${OPTIONAL_TABLES[@]}"; do
+    IFS='|' read -r o_name o_heading <<< "$entry"
+    if [[ "$o_name" == "$section" ]]; then

+# Removes an optional table block from FILE: the exact heading line, the
+# table-header lines between it and the start marker, the marker block, and
+# one blank line after the end marker. A file without the start marker is
+# already pruned (no-op). Anything else between the heading and the start
+# marker, a missing heading or a missing end marker is an error and leaves
+# FILE untouched.
+prune_optional_table() {
+  local file="$1" section="$2" heading="$3"
+  if ! grep -q "@constraint-generated: start ${section} " "$file"; then
+    verbose "Optional section ${section} already absent from ${file}"
+    return 0
+  fi

+  awk -v heading="$heading" \
+      -v start="@constraint-generated: start ${section} " \
+      -v end="@constraint-generated: end ${section} " '

+    }
+    state == "skip" { if (index($0, end)) state = "after"; next }
+    state == "after" { state = "done"; if ($0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*$/) next }
+    { print }
+    END {
+      if (state == "head") flush()
+      if (state == "skip") exit 3
+      if (state == "" ) exit 4
+    }
+  ' "$file" > "$tmp" || rc=$?
+  if [[ "$rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
+    rm -f "$tmp"
+    case "$rc" in

+      4) log "ERROR: ${file}: optional section '${section}' has markers but no '${heading}' heading directly above its table" ;;
+      *) log "ERROR: ${file}: pruning optional section '${section}' failed (awk exit ${rc})" ;;
+    esac

     6	# No profile can reach the floor. The floor source is .claude/data/floor.yaml
     7	# (read here, never duplicated); its sha256 pin is READ from
     8	# tests/unit/guard-origins.bats (FLOOR_SHA256) so the two suites cannot

    10	# `standard`: the floor config keys (the two gate skills' flatline_protocol.*
    11	# config, destructive_command_guard.*, implement_gate.*, hounfour.locality),
    12	# verdict-derive.sh on fixture feedback files, the adversarial gate's

    14	# the FR-1.2b / FR-SZ probes, and user-invoked-commands.txt.

    36	
    37	@test "PF-1 floor.yaml matches the sha256 pin guard-origins.bats carries (one constant, two suites)" {

    47	import re, subprocess, sys, json

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/lint-invariants.bats — cycle-129 D-4.5 (AC-2.5)
#
# The five C-TEAM rows left constraints.json; generate-constraints.sh omits the
# "## Agent Teams" table when the class is empty and renders it when rows
# exist; lint-invariants.sh fails when the kernel and the registry disagree.
# The generator runs against a fixture tree (it resolves its inputs relative
# to the working directory), never against the live kernel.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    GEN="$R/.claude/scripts/generate-constraints.sh"
    LINT="$R/.claude/scripts/lint-invariants.sh"
    F="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/tree"
    mkdir -p "$F/.claude/loa" "$F/.claude/data" "$F/.claude/templates"
    cp -R "$R/.claude/templates/constraints" "$F/.claude/templates/constraints"
    cp "$R/.claude/data/constraints.json" "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json"
    cp "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
}

# A kernel that still carries the pre-cycle-129 Agent Teams block, placed
# between the merge constraints and the Agent-Network section as it was.
add_team_block() {
    python3 -I - "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" <<'PY'
import sys
p = sys.argv[1]
s = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
anchor = "## Agent-Network Primitives"
block = ("## Agent Teams\n\n| Rule | Why |\n|------|-----|\n"
         "<!-- @constraint-generated: start agent_teams_constraints | hash:0000000000000000 -->\n"
         "<!-- DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/constraints.json -->\n"
         "| MUST stale row | stale |\n"
         "<!-- @constraint-generated: end agent_teams_constraints -->\n\n")
assert s.count(anchor) == 1
open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s.replace(anchor, block + anchor))
PY
}

add_team_row() {
    jq '.constraints += [{"id":"C-TEAM-901","name":"fixture_row","category":"agent_teams","rule_type":"MUST",
        "text":"fixture rule","text_variants":{"claude-loa-md":"MUST fixture rule"},"why":"fixture why","order":0,
        "layers":[{"target":"claude-loa-md","section":"agent_teams_constraints","render_as":"table_row"}],
        "severity":"low","source_incident":"#0"}]' "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json" > "$F/c.json"
    mv "$F/c.json" "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json"
}

gen() { (cd "$F" && bash "$GEN" --section "${1:-agent_teams_constraints}"); }

@test "LI-1 constraints.json carries no C-TEAM rows and no agent_teams_constraints layer" {
    run jq '[.constraints[] | select((.id | startswith("C-TEAM")) or any(.layers[]?; .section == "agent_teams_constraints"))] | length' \
        "$R/.claude/data/constraints.json"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ "$output" = "0" ]
}

@test "LI-2 the live kernel carries neither the Agent Teams heading nor its marker" {
    ! grep -qxF '## Agent Teams' "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    ! grep -q 'agent_teams_constraints' "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
}

@test "LI-3 the generator removes a leftover Agent Teams block when the class is empty" {
    add_team_block
    grep -qxF '## Agent Teams' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    run gen
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    ! grep -qxF '## Agent Teams' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    ! grep -q 'agent_teams_constraints' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    # The neighbouring sections survive with one blank line between them.
    grep -qF '<!-- @constraint-generated: end merge_constraints -->' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    run grep -c '^## Agent-Network Primitives$' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    [ "$output" = "1" ]
    run diff <(sed -n '/end merge_constraints/,/^## Agent-Network/p' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md") \
             <(printf '%s\n' '<!-- @constraint-generated: end merge_constraints -->' '' '## Agent-Network Primitives')
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
}

@test "LI-4 pruning is idempotent: a second run leaves the kernel byte-identical" {
    add_team_block
    gen
    cp "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/first.md"
    run gen
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    cmp "$F/first.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
}

@test "LI-5 the generator renders the table when the class has rows" {
    add_team_block
    add_team_row
    run gen
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    grep -qxF '## Agent Teams' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    grep -qxF '| MUST fixture rule | fixture why |' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    ! grep -qF 'MUST stale row' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
}

@test "LI-6 rows without the heading block fail loudly and leave the kernel untouched" {
    add_team_row
    cp "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/before.md"
    run gen
    [ "$status" -ne 0 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"Missing markers"*"agent_teams_constraints"* ]]
    cmp "$F/before.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
}

@test "LI-7 a marker block with foreign text above it is an error, not a silent deletion" {
    add_team_block
    python3 -I - "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" <<'PY'
import sys
p = sys.argv[1]
s = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
s = s.replace("## Agent Teams\n\n| Rule | Why |", "## Agent Teams\n\nOperator prose that is not a table.\n\n| Rule | Why |")
open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s)
PY
    cp "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/before.md"
    run gen
    [ "$status" -ne 0 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"no '## Agent Teams' heading directly above its table"* ]]
    cmp "$F/before.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
}

@test "LI-8 lint-invariants passes the optional-table invariant on the live tree" {
    run bash -c "cd '$R' && bash '$LINT' --json"
    echo "$output" | jq -e '.results[] | select(.message | test("agent_teams_constraints: table presence matches"))' >/dev/null
    ! echo "$output" | jq -e '.results[] | select(.level == "ERROR" and (.message | test("agent_teams")))' >/dev/null
    # The field name is load-bearing: the negative check above is vacuous if
    # the report shape ever renames `level`.
    echo "$output" | jq -e '[.results[] | has("level")] | all' >/dev/null
}

@test "LI-9 the lint self-test (test-lint-invariants.sh) is green" {
    run bash -c "cd '$R' && bash .claude/scripts/test-lint-invariants.sh"
    echo "$output" | tail -3
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

for entry in "${SECTIONS[@]}"; do
    local s_name s_target s_template s_filter
    IFS='|' read -r s_name s_target s_template s_filter <<< "$entry"

    if [[ -n "$SECTION_FILTER" ]] && [[ "$s_name" != "$SECTION_FILTER" ]]; then
      continue
    fi

    if [[ ! -f "$s_target" ]]; then
      log "WARNING: Target file not found: $s_target, skipping"
      continue
    fi

    target_sections["$s_target"]+="${s_name} "
    section_data["$s_name"]="${s_target}|${s_template}|${s_filter}"
  done

  if [[ ${#target_sections[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
    log "No sections to generate"
    return 0
  fi

  # Phase 1: Create staged copies
  declare -A staged_files
  trap 'for tmp in "${staged_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$tmp"; done' EXIT

  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp "${target}.constraint-XXXXXX")
    cp "$target" "$tmp"
    staged_files["$target"]="$tmp"
  done

  # Phase 2: Render and apply all sections to staged copies
  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    local tmp="${staged_files[$target]}"
    for section in ${target_sections[$target]}; do
      local s_data="${section_data[$section]}"
      local s_target s_template s_filter
      IFS='|' read -r s_target s_template s_filter <<< "$s_data"

      local o_heading
      if o_heading=$(optional_table_heading "$section"); then
        local o_rows
        o_rows=$(jq -r "$s_filter | length" "$REGISTRY")
        if [[ "$o_rows" == "0" ]]; then
          if [[ "$BOOTSTRAP" != "true" ]] && ! prune_optional_table "$tmp" "$section" "$o_heading"; then
            log "ERROR: Generation failed for section '${section}' — no files modified"
            return 1
          fi
          continue
        fi
      fi

      verbose "Rendering section: $section"
      local content
      content=$(render_section "$section" "$s_template" "$s_filter")

      if [[ "$BOOTSTRAP" == "true" ]]; then
        bootstrap_section "$tmp" "$section" "$content"
      else
        if ! insert_generated_section "$tmp" "$section" "$content"; then
          log "ERROR: Generation failed for section '${section}' — no files modified"
          return 1
        fi
      fi
    done
  done

  # Phase 3: Diff or commit
  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]] && [[ "$BOOTSTRAP_CONFIRM" != "true" ]]; then
    for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
      log "Diff for ${target}:"
      diff -u "$target" "${staged_files[$target]}" || true
    done
    for tmp in "${staged_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$tmp"; done
    trap - EXIT
    return 0
  fi

  # Commit with rollback
  declare -A backup_files
  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    local bak="${target}.constraint-bak"
    cp "$target" "$bak"
    backup_files["$target"]="$bak"
  done

  local commit_failed=false
  local committed=()
  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    if mv "${staged_files[$target]}" "$target"; then
      committed+=("$target")
    else
      commit_failed=true
      break
    fi
  done

  if [[ "$commit_failed" == "true" ]]; then
    local rollback_ok=true
    for t in "${committed[@]}"; do
      if ! cp -f "${backup_files[$t]}" "$t"; then
        rollback_ok=false
      fi
    done
    for tmp in "${staged_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$tmp"; done
    if [[ "$rollback_ok" == "true" ]]; then
      for bak in "${backup_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$bak"; done
      log "ERROR: Commit failed — all targets rolled back"
    else
      log "ERROR: Commit failed — rollback partially failed, .constraint-bak files preserved"
    fi
    trap - EXIT
    return 1
  fi

  # Success: clean up backups and update @loa-managed hashes
  for bak in "${backup_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$bak"; done
  trap - EXIT

  # Phase 4: Update @loa-managed hashes (IMP-002)
  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    if bash "$MARKER_UTILS" has-marker "$target" | grep -q "true"; then
      verbose "Updating @loa-managed hash for ${target}"
      bash "$MARKER_UTILS" update-hash "$target"
    fi
  done

  log "Generation complete: ${#target_sections[@]} target(s) updated"

--- a/base/.claude/scripts/validate-skill-capabilities.sh
+++ b/head/.claude/scripts/validate-skill-capabilities.sh
@@ -87,7 +87,12 @@ VALID_EFFORTS=("low" "medium" "high" "xhigh" "max")
 # "no application code" boundary is enforced by ZONES, not by removing Write.
 # Adding a new write-capable review skill is intentionally a one-line edit here
 # with reviewer visibility (mirrors WRITE_CAPABLE_AGENTS).
-REVIEW_WRITE_EXCEPTIONS=("red-teaming" "bridgebuilder-review" "spiraling" "autonomous-agent" "run-bridge" "run-mode" "reviewing-code" "auditing-security")
+# rtfm-testing (cycle-129 D-4.2): writes its Phase 4 report under
+# grimoires/loa/a2a/rtfm/; Edit and NotebookEdit are disallowed.
+REVIEW_WRITE_EXCEPTIONS=("red-teaming" "bridgebuilder-review" "spiraling" "autonomous-agent" "run-bridge" "run-mode" "reviewing-code" "auditing-security" "rtfm-testing")
+# cycle-129 D-4.2: a pure-review skill (role: review, capabilities.write_files:
+# false) must remove all three write tools through disallowed-tools.
+PURE_REVIEW_STRIP=("Write" "Edit" "NotebookEdit")
 
 # Review-class keywords for heuristic linter (SDD §20.5 ATK-A13)
 # Skills declaring role: review|audit MUST have >=2 of these in body
@@ -614,6 +619,22 @@ validate_skill() {
                 log_warning "$skill_name" "role: review with capabilities.write_files: true but Write not in disallowed-tools and not a documented write-exception — C-PROC-001 is enforced only by prose (cycle-114 FR-4)" || has_error=true
             fi
         fi
+        # --- cycle-129 D-4.2: a pure-review skill strips the write tools ---
+        # Read without `//` (yq's alternative operator treats an explicit
+        # false as absent); accept the list or the comma-string form.
+        local pr_wf pr_dis pr_missing="" pr_t
+        pr_wf=$(echo "$frontmatter" | yq eval '.capabilities.write_files' - 2>/dev/null) || pr_wf="null"
+        if [[ "$pr_wf" == "false" ]]; then
+            pr_dis=$(echo "$frontmatter" | yq eval '.disallowed-tools | ((select(tag == "!!seq") | join(",")) // .)' - 2>/dev/null) || pr_dis=""
+            [[ "$pr_dis" == "null" ]] && pr_dis=""
+            for pr_t in "${PURE_REVIEW_STRIP[@]}"; do
+                has_tool "$pr_dis" "$pr_t" || pr_missing+="${pr_missing:+, }$pr_t"
+            done
+            if [[ -n "$pr_missing" ]]; then
+                log_error "$skill_name" "pure-review skill (role: review, capabilities.write_files: false) must carry disallowed-tools: Write, Edit, NotebookEdit — missing: ${pr_missing} (cycle-129 D-4.2)"
+                has_error=true
+            fi
+        fi
     fi
 
     # --- Agent type vs write-capability invariant (Issue #553) ---

   schema_version: 1
   read_files: true
@@ -906,3 +909,125 @@ cost-profile: moderate
     run "$VALIDATOR" --help
     [[ "$output" == *"--agent-types-file"* ]]
 }
+
+# =========================================================================
+# cycle-129 D-4.2 (AC-2.2): a pure-review skill (role: review,
+# capabilities.write_files: false) strips Write, Edit and NotebookEdit
+# =========================================================================
+
+# pure_review_skill <name> [disallowed-tools block lines...]
+pure_review_skill() {
+    local name="$1"; shift
+    local dis=""
+    [[ $# -gt 0 ]] && dis="$(printf '%s\n' "$@")"
+    create_skill "$name" "---
+name: $name
+description: pure review fixture
+role: review
+allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob
+${dis}
+capabilities:
+  schema_version: 1
+  read_files: true
+  search_code: true
+  write_files: false
+  execute_commands: false
+  web_access: false
+  user_interaction: false
+  agent_spawn: false
+  task_management: false
+cost-profile: lightweight
+---
+# Pure review: review and verify findings"
+}
+
+@test "c129-D4.2: a pure-review skill without disallowed-tools fails by name" {
+    pure_review_skill bare-review
+    SKILLS_DIR="$FIXTURE_DIR" run "$VALIDATOR" --skill bare-review
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"pure-review skill (role: review, capabilities.write_files: false) must carry disallowed-tools: Write, Edit, NotebookEdit — missing: Write, Edit, NotebookEdit"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "c129-D4.2: a pure-review skill missing one of the three fails naming it" {
+    pure_review_skill partial-review "disallowed-tools:" "  - Write" "  - Edit"
+    SKILLS_DIR="$FIXTURE_DIR" run "$VALIDATOR" --skill partial-review --json
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    echo "$output" | jq -e '.results[] | select(.skill == "partial-review" and .level == "error" and (.message | endswith("missing: NotebookEdit (cycle-129 D-4.2)")))' >/dev/null
+}
+
+@test "c129-D4.2: the strip passes in list form and in comma-string form" {
+    pure_review_skill list-review "disallowed-tools:" "  - Write" "  - Edit" "  - NotebookEdit"
+    SKILLS_DIR="$FIXTURE_DIR" run "$VALIDATOR" --skill list-review
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" != *"pure-review skill"* ]]
+    pure_review_skill string-review "disallowed-tools: Write, Edit, NotebookEdit"
+    SKILLS_DIR="$FIXTURE_DIR" run "$VALIDATOR" --skill string-review
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" != *"pure-review skill"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "c129-D4.2: an explicit write_files: false is read as false (not through yq's //)" {
+    # A review skill that declares write_files: true is outside the rule.
+    create_skill "writer-review" "---
+name: writer-review
+description: report writer fixture
+role: review
+allowed-tools: Read, Write
+disallowed-tools:
+  - Write
+capabilities:
+  schema_version: 1
+  read_files: true
+  search_code: true
+  write_files: true
+  execute_commands: false
+  web_access: false
+  user_interaction: false
+  agent_spawn: false
+  task_management: false
+cost-profile: moderate
+---
+# Writer review: review findings"
+    SKILLS_DIR="$FIXTURE_DIR" run "$VALIDATOR" --skill writer-review
+    [[ "$output" != *"pure-review skill"* ]]
+    pure_review_skill bare-review2
+    SKILLS_DIR="$FIXTURE_DIR" run "$VALIDATOR" --skill bare-review2
+    [[ "$output" == *"pure-review skill"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "c129-D4.2: the three pure-review skills carry the strip; rtfm-testing is a report author" {
+    local s fm
+    for s in eval-running flatline-knowledge validating-construct-manifest; do
+        fm=$(awk '/^---$/{if(n++) exit; next} n' "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/skills/$s/SKILL.md" | yq -o=json '.')
+        echo "$fm" | jq -e '.role == "review" and .capabilities.write_files == false
+            and ((."disallowed-tools" | sort) == ["Edit","NotebookEdit","Write"])' >/dev/null || { echo "$s"; return 1; }
+        run "$VALIDATOR" --skill "$s"
+        [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    done
+    # rtfm-testing writes its Phase 4 report (grimoires/loa/a2a/rtfm/), so it
+    # keeps Write and strips the other two.
+    fm=$(awk '/^---$/{if(n++) exit; next} n' "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/skills/rtfm-testing/SKILL.md" | yq -o=json '.')
+    echo "$fm" | jq -e '.capabilities.write_files == true and (."disallowed-tools" | sort) == ["Edit","NotebookEdit"]
+        and (."allowed-tools" | contains("Write"))' >/dev/null
+    grep -q 'grimoires/loa/a2a/rtfm/report-' "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/skills/rtfm-testing/SKILL.md"
+    run "$VALIDATOR" --skill rtfm-testing --strict
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "c129-D4.2: every role: review skill with write_files: false in the tree carries the strip" {
+    local f fm n=0
+    for f in "$PROJECT_ROOT"/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md; do
+        fm=$(awk '/^---$/{if(n++) exit; next} n' "$f" | yq -o=json '.' 2>/dev/null) || continue
+        if echo "$fm" | jq -e '.role == "review" and .capabilities.write_files == false' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+            n=$((n + 1))
+            echo "$fm" | jq -e '(."disallowed-tools" // []) as $d | ["Write","Edit","NotebookEdit"] | all(. as $t | $d | index($t))' >/dev/null \
+                || { echo "$f lacks the strip"; return 1; }
+        fi
+    done
+    [ "$n" -ge 3 ]
+}
+
+@test "c129-D4.2: skill-invariants.md names the Bash gap" {
+    tr '\n' ' ' < "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/rules/skill-invariants.md" | grep -qi 'shell-redirection writes remain fence territory'
+    grep -q 'eval-running' "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/rules/skill-invariants.md"
+}

diff --git a/base/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh b/head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh

--- a/base/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh
+++ b/head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh
@@ -5,20 +5,45 @@
 # Checks whether Write/Edit to App Zone files occurs within an active
 # /implement or /bug skill invocation.
 #
-# Two detection modes:
-#   1. HEURISTIC (ADVISORY, the default): reads .run/ state files for RUNNING state
-#   2. AUTHORITATIVE: reads tool_input.active_skill from hook stdin, only when
-#      .loa.config.yaml sets implement_gate.mode: authoritative. The PreToolUse
+# Modes (cycle-129 D-4.1, DEC-0163; .loa.config.yaml implement_gate.mode):
+#   ask (default; unset or any other value): an unsanctioned App-Zone write asks,
+#       exactly as before, and now logs one row (decision "ask").
+#   telemetry: an unsanctioned App-Zone write logs one row (action "telemetry",
+#       decision "outside_run") and is allowed silently.
+#   deny: an unsanctioned App-Zone write is DENIED when the run position is
+#       known: .run/sprint-plan-state.json parses and its derived_at is within
+#       run_mode.stale_hours (12). The gate is a fence only in this mode. An
+#       unknown position (cache missing, not derived, stale or unparseable)
+#       falls back to ask (decision "unknown_position"), never to allow.
+# Sanction (any mode; first match wins; one row each, action "allow"):
+#   sanctioned_run    — the heuristic below: a fresh RUNNING cache, and its
+#                       derived_at (when present) within run_mode.stale_hours
+#   sanctioned_marker — .run/implement-active.json {skill: implement|bug, sprint,
+#                       started_at} with started_at within two hours (written by
+#                       `run-checkpoint.sh mark`, removed by `unmark`); a stale or
+#                       malformed marker logs decision "stale_marker" and does not sanction
+#   override          — LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE=1 in the hook's environment
+# Rows go to .run/audit.jsonl as {ts, hook: "implement-gate", action, decision,
+# mode, path} with path control-stripped and cut to 256 bytes; LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
+# adds replay: true to every row this gate writes (DEC-0167).
+#
+# Claims modifier (implement_gate.claims: authoritative; the legacy
+# implement_gate.mode: authoritative means mode ask + claims authoritative):
+#   reads tool_input.active_skill from hook stdin. The PreToolUse
 #      payload carries no harness-set skill field (cycle-126 D-4.4) and tool_input
-#      is model-authored, so nothing in .run/ selects this mode.
+#      is model-authored, so nothing in .run/ selects this modifier.
 #      TIGHTEN-ONLY (sprint-250 audit n17/n18): the model-authored claim can only
 #      add an ask, never grant an allow. A claimed implementation skill falls
 #      through to the heuristic exactly like an absent field; a claimed
-#      non-implementation skill asks and logs compliance.mode.model_signal to
+#      non-implementation skill asks (or, under deny with a known position and no
+#      sanction, is denied) and logs compliance.mode.model_signal to
 #      .run/audit.jsonl (plain hook log, not the signed audit_emit chain). Every
-#      claim leaves one row per invocation: decision "ask" for a non-implementation
+#      claim leaves one row per invocation: decision "ask"/"deny" for a non-implementation
 #      claim, decision "heuristic" for an implementation claim (run-2 finding 6).
 #
+# `implement-gate.sh --effective-mode [CONFIG]` prints the effective mode (and the
+# claims modifier) without reading stdin — the /loa Gate line.
+#
 # Evidence recorder (cycle-126 D-4.4): a lead-session payload carrying
 # tool_input.active_skill records active_skill_seen_at once in
 # .run/platform-features.json. It is evidence only and never changes the mode.
@@ -33,13 +58,15 @@
 # (<root>/.claude/hooks/compliance/), never the process cwd, which follows
 # Claude's `cd` (audit MED-001); RUN_DIR defaults to <root>/.run.
 # Trust inputs: a write to .run/state.json, .run/sprint-plan-state.json,
-# .run/simstim-state.json, .run/platform-features.json, .run/audit.jsonl or
-# .loa.config.yaml asks and logs compliance.state_write (run-3 finding 3).
+# .run/simstim-state.json, .run/platform-features.json, .run/audit.jsonl,
+# .run/implement-active.json or .loa.config.yaml asks in every mode and under
+# every sanction, and logs compliance.state_write (run-3 finding 3).
 # Other non-App-Zone writes always allowed.

 # Output (Claude Code PreToolUse contract, sprint-250 audit n20): allow = silent

@@ -58,8 +85,11 @@
 # Sprint-108 T4.5: Path normalization

-# Read tool input from stdin
-input=$(cat 2>/dev/null) || input=""
+# Read tool input from stdin (not for --effective-mode, which reads no payload)
+input=""

+    input=$(cat 2>/dev/null) || input=""
+fi
 
 # The ask reply; jq builds it so any reason is a well-formed JSON string (run-3 finding 7); the printf literal is only

@@ -145,6 +175,44 @@ PROJECT_ROOT="${PROJECT_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOUR
 RUN_DIR="${RUN_DIR:-$PROJECT_ROOT/.run}"
 FEATURES_FILE="$RUN_DIR/platform-features.json"
 
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Mode and claims (cycle-129 D-4.1): one yq call, read only when a decision
+# needs it. Unset, unreadable or unknown values are ask; the legacy
+# mode: authoritative is ask + claims: authoritative. run_mode.stale_hours

+gate_claims="plain"

# Sets the variable named $1 to at most 256 bytes of $2, never ending inside a UTF-8 character: a trailing lead byte
# whose sequence the cut left short, or stray continuation bytes, are dropped (run-3 finding 5; jq would read a split
# character as U+FFFD). printf -v, not $(...), so a trailing newline in a raw value survives into the audit row
cut_utf8_256() {
    local LC_ALL=C
    local _c_s=${2:0:256} _c_n _c_i _c_b _c_need
    _c_n=${#_c_s}
    for (( _c_i = _c_n - 1; _c_i >= 0 && _c_i >= _c_n - 4; _c_i-- )); do
        printf -v _c_b '%d' "'${_c_s:_c_i:1}"
        (( _c_b >= 128 && _c_b < 192 )) && continue   # continuation byte: keep walking back to its lead
        if (( _c_b < 128 )); then _c_need=1; elif (( _c_b < 224 )); then _c_need=2; elif (( _c_b < 240 )); then _c_need=3; else _c_need=4; fi
        if (( _c_n - _c_i < _c_need )); then _c_s=${_c_s:0:_c_i}          # the cut left this character short
        elif (( _c_n - _c_i > _c_need )); then _c_s=${_c_s:0:_c_i+_c_need}   # continuation bytes after a complete character are stray
        fi
        printf -v "$1" '%s' "$_c_s"
        return 0
    done
    printf -v "$1" '%s' "${_c_s:0:_c_i+1}"   # only continuation bytes at the end: drop them
}

# Display copy of a model-authored string: cut to 256 bytes first (the fixed point below then costs at most a few
# passes over a short string), then C0 and DEL, then the sequences above byte-wise until nothing changes (deleting
# one sequence can join its neighbours into another: C2 C2 9B 9B)
strip_controls() {
    local LC_ALL=C s prev seq

# Heuristic mode: Is an /implement or /bug skill currently active?
# Check .run/sprint-plan-state.json, .run/simstim-state.json, .run/state.json
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# True when the ISO-8601 timestamp $1 parses and is within 24 h (86400 s) of now, either side; empty or unparsable is stale
# (sprint-250 audit LOW-004: tighten-only; LOW-006: a future-dated stamp is not fresh forever)
_ig_fresh() {
    [[ -n "$1" ]] || return 1
    local now last_epoch
    now=$(date +%s 2>/dev/null) || return 1
    if type _date_to_epoch &>/dev/null; then
        last_epoch=$(_date_to_epoch "$1" 2>/dev/null) || last_epoch=""
    else
        last_epoch=$(date -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null || date -jf '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null) || last_epoch=""
    fi
    [[ "$last_epoch" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
    (( last_epoch > 0 && now - last_epoch <= 86400 && last_epoch - now <= 86400 ))
}

# True when the ISO-8601 timestamp $2 parses, is at most $1 seconds old and at most 300 s ahead (clock skew);
# jq's fromdateiso8601 keeps it portable (no GNU date -d). Fractional seconds are dropped first
_ig_within() {
    [[ -n "$2" && "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
    jq -en --arg t "$2" --argjson w "$1" \
        '($t | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) as $e | $e != null and (now - $e) <= $w and ($e - now) <= 300' \
        >/dev/null 2>&1
}

# derived_at, when a cache carries one, must be within run_mode.stale_hours (cycle-129 D-4.1)
_ig_derived_ok() {
    local da
    da=$(jq -r '.derived_at // empty | strings' "$1" 2>/dev/null) || da=""
    [[ -z "$da" ]] && return 0
    _ig_within $(( gate_stale_hours * 3600 )) "$da"
}

check_implementation_active() {
    # Check sprint-plan state
    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" ]]; then
        local state plan_id last_activity
        state=$(jq -r '.state // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
        plan_id=$(jq -r '.plan_id // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || true

        # Integrity: must have plan_id
        if [[ -z "$plan_id" ]]; then
            return 1
        fi

        # Integrity: check staleness (within 24 h either side, via _ig_fresh); an absent or unparsable
        # last_activity is stale too (sprint-250 audit LOW-006: the check was skipped, so RUNNING + plan_id allowed)
        last_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || last_activity=""
        if ! _ig_fresh "$last_activity"; then
            return 1  # Stale, future-dated or unstamped state
        fi

        # A derived cache older than run_mode.stale_hours is not a run position (cycle-129 D-4.1)
        if ! _ig_derived_ok "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json"; then
            return 1
        fi

        if [[ "$state" == "RUNNING" ]]; then
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Check simstim state; its writers (simstim-state.sh, simstim-orchestrator.sh) stamp .timestamps.last_activity,
    # and a stale or unstamped file falls through (LOW-004)
    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" ]]; then
        local phase simstim_activity
        phase=$(jq -r '.phase // empty' "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
        simstim_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // empty | strings' "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || simstim_activity=""
        if [[ "$phase" == "implementation" ]] && _ig_fresh "$simstim_activity"; then
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Check run state; run-mode stamps .timestamps.last_activity (state-schemas.md), .updated_at is the fallback
    # run-preflight.sh reads too; a stale or unstamped file falls through (LOW-004)
    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/state.json" ]]; then
        local run_state run_activity
        run_state=$(jq -r '.state // empty' "$RUN_DIR/state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
        run_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // .updated_at // empty | strings' "$RUN_DIR/state.json" 2>/dev/null) || run_activity=""
        if [[ "$run_state" == "RUNNING" ]] && _ig_fresh "$run_activity" && _ig_derived_ok "$RUN_DIR/state.json"; then
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    return 1
}

_loa_pl_write_cache() {
  [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -n "$_LOA_PL_JSON" ]] || return 0
  local dir="${_LOA_PL_CACHE%/*}" tmp

# Loads the resolved document into _LOA_PL_JSON (memo → cache → build).
# Returns 1 when it cannot be resolved (jq or yq missing).
_loa_pl_load() {
  _loa_pl_paths

  if [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_JSON" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && "$_LOA_PL_ID" == "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" ]]; then

  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
  if [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -f "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]]; then

    fi

  _LOA_PL_ID="$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID"
  _loa_pl_write_cache
  return 0
}

# Live read of one explicit key (non-profile keys, or no resolution available).
_loa_pl_live() {
  local key="$1" fallback="$2" v
  if [[ -f "${_LOA_PL_CFG:-}" ]] && command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    v=$(yq -o=json ".$key" "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'if . == null then "__LOA_PL_MISS__" elif type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end' 2>/dev/null) || v=""
    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$v"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
  return 0
}

loa_knob() {
  local path="${1:-}" fallback="${2:-}" key v
  key="${path#.}"
  if [[ ! "$key" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ ]]; then
    _loa_pl_warn "loa_knob: malformed key path '${path//[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/?}'"
    printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
    return 2
  fi
  # Warm path: one stat + one jq straight from the cache file.
  _loa_pl_paths
  _loa_pl_id
  if [[ -z "$_LOA_PL_JSON" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -f "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]] &&
     command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    v=$(jq -r --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" --arg k "$key" '
          if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then
            (if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value

          else "__LOA_PL_STALE__" end' "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_STALE__"

      _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
      return 0
    fi

      printf '%s\n' "$v"
      return 0
    fi

  if ! _loa_pl_load; then
    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
    return 0
  fi

    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"

@test "#961 K-1: hook exits 0 with no stdin (graceful degradation)" {
    run bash -c "echo '' | '$HOOK'"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
}

@test "#961 K-1: hook respects surgical_diff_warning:false (no state file written)" {
    cat > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE" <<EOF
karpathy_principles:
  surgical_diff_warning: false
EOF
    local input
    input="$(_write_input "line1
line2
line3
line4
line5
line6")"
    run bash -c "echo '$input' | '$HOOK'"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ ! -f "$KARPATHY_TASK_STATE" ]
}

@test "#961 K-1: hook accumulates lines across multiple invocations" {
    local input
    input="$(_write_input "a
b
c")"
    run bash -c "echo '$input' | '$HOOK'"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ -f "$KARPATHY_TASK_STATE" ]
    local n
    n=$(wc -l < "$KARPATHY_TASK_STATE")
    [ "$n" -eq 1 ]

    # Second invocation appends, doesn't overwrite
    run bash -c "echo '$input' | '$HOOK'"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    n=$(wc -l < "$KARPATHY_TASK_STATE")
    [ "$n" -eq 2 ]
}

    local content="a

    run bash -c "echo '$input' | '$HOOK' 2>&1"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

}

for e in "${VALID_EFFORTS[@]}"; do
            [[ "$effort" == "$e" ]] && effort_valid=true && break
        done
        if [[ "$effort_valid" == "false" ]]; then
            log_error "$skill_name" "Invalid effort '$effort' (must be one of: ${VALID_EFFORTS[*]}) — cycle-114 FR-3"
            has_error=true
        elif [[ "$cp" == "lightweight" && ( "$effort" == "xhigh" || "$effort" == "max" ) ]]; then
            log_warning "$skill_name" "cost-profile: lightweight but effort: $effort (deep reasoning on a cheap-tier skill — correlation mismatch)" || has_error=true
        fi
    fi

    # --- cycle-114 FR-4: review skills must mechanically disallow Write ---
    # A role:review skill that can write_files but neither disallows Write nor
    # is a documented write-exception leaves C-PROC-001 ("no application code
    # outside /implement") enforced only by prose. Surface that gap as a WARN.
    local fr4_role
    fr4_role=$(echo "$frontmatter" | yq eval '.role // ""' - 2>/dev/null) || fr4_role=""
    if [[ "$fr4_role" == "review" ]]; then
        local fr4_wf
        fr4_wf=$(echo "$frontmatter" | yq eval '.capabilities.write_files // "null"' - 2>/dev/null) || fr4_wf="null"
        if [[ "$fr4_wf" == "true" ]]; then
            local disallowed
            disallowed=$(echo "$frontmatter" | yq eval '(.disallowed-tools // []) | join(",")' - 2>/dev/null) || disallowed=""
            local is_exception=false
            local x
            for x in "${REVIEW_WRITE_EXCEPTIONS[@]}"; do
                [[ "$skill_name" == "$x" ]] && is_exception=true && break
            done
            if [[ "$is_exception" == "false" ]] && ! has_tool "$disallowed" "Write"; then
                log_warning "$skill_name" "role: review with capabilities.write_files: true but Write not in disallowed-tools and not a documented write-exception — C-PROC-001 is enforced only by prose (cycle-114 FR-4)" || has_error=true
            fi
        fi
        # --- cycle-129 D-4.2: a pure-review skill strips the write tools ---
        # Read without `//` (yq's alternative operator treats an explicit
        # false as absent); accept the list or the comma-string form.
        local pr_wf pr_dis pr_missing="" pr_t
        pr_wf=$(echo "$frontmatter" | yq eval '.capabilities.write_files' - 2>/dev/null) || pr_wf="null"
        if [[ "$pr_wf" == "false" ]]; then
            pr_dis=$(echo "$frontmatter" | yq eval '.disallowed-tools | ((select(tag == "!!seq") | join(",")) // .)' - 2>/dev/null) || pr_dis=""

                has_error=true
            fi

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/prompt-budget.bats — cycle-124 FR-8 / AC-8.1
#
# tools/check-prompt-budget.sh enforces the byte budgets of the always-loaded
# prompt surface: SKILL.md ≤ 16,384 B (charged with unconditionally-read
# resources), CLAUDE.loa.md ≤ 9,445 B (cycle-129 D-3.3: measured 9,189 B + 256 B;
# the cap only ever falls), protocols total ≤ 160,000 B (warn above 114,688 B).
# Passes at exactly the limit, fails one byte over.
# PB-10 pins the workflow's header comment to the tool's constants.
# PB-9 is the live gate: red until the Sprint 3 audit lands.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
    SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    TOOL="$PROJECT_ROOT/tools/check-prompt-budget.sh"
    T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/pb.XXXXXX")"
    mkdir -p "$T/.claude/skills/s1/resources" "$T/.claude/loa" "$T/.claude/protocols"
    P="$T/.claude/protocols"
    fill "$T/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" 100
    fill "$P/a.md" 100
}

teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }

fill() {  # fill <path> <bytes> — exactly <bytes> bytes of text
    head -c "$2" /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'x' > "$1"
}

@test "PB-1 a SKILL.md of exactly 16,384 bytes passes" {
    fill "$T/.claude/skills/s1/SKILL.md" 16384
    run "$TOOL" --root "$T" --quiet
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
}

@test "PB-2 a SKILL.md of 16,385 bytes fails and the breach names the skill and the byte count" {
    fill "$T/.claude/skills/s1/SKILL.md" 16385
    run "$TOOL" --root "$T"
    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"skill s1: 16385 B > 16384 B"* ]]
}

@test "PB-3 an unguarded read imperative charges the resource; a guarded pointer does not" {
    fill "$T/.claude/skills/s1/resources/REFERENCE.md" 1000
    { fill /dev/stdout 15500; printf '\nRead `resources/REFERENCE.md` before starting.\n'; } > "$T/.claude/skills/s1/SKILL.md"
    run "$TOOL" --root "$T" --json
    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.skills[0].charged_resources | length')" = "1" ]
    [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.skills[0].charged_resources[0].bytes')" = "1000" ]
    { fill /dev/stdout 15500; printf '\nSee `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Security if you need the checklist.\n'; } > "$T/.claude/skills/s1/SKILL.md"
    run "$TOOL" --root "$T" --json
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.skills[0].charged_resources | length')" = "0" ]
}

@test "PB-4 CLAUDE.loa.md passes at 9,445 bytes and fails at 9,446 (cycle-129 D-3.3 cap: measured kernel + 256 B; the cycle-126 replay A/B kept the rationales, cycle-129 removed the Agent Teams table)" {
    fill "$T/.claude/skills/s1/SKILL.md" 100
    fill "$T/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" 9445
    run "$TOOL" --root "$T" --quiet
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    fill "$T/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" 9446
    run "$TOOL" --root "$T"
    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"CLAUDE.loa.md: 9446 B > 9445 B"* ]]
}

@test "PB-5 protocols: above 114,688 warns but passes; above 160,000 fails; reference/ is not counted" {
    fill "$T/.claude/skills/s1/SKILL.md" 100
    fill "$P/a.md" 100000
    fill "$P/b.md" 20000
    mkdir -p "$P/reference"; fill "$P/reference/moved.md" 90000

    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.protocols.warn')" = "true" ]

name: Prompt Budget

# cycle-124 FR-8 (AC-8.1): the always-loaded prompt surface has hard byte
# budgets — SKILL.md ≤ 16,384 B (charged with unconditionally-read resources),
# CLAUDE.loa.md ≤ 9,445 B, protocols total ≤ 160,000 B (warn > 114,688 B).
# tools/check-prompt-budget.sh is the gate; the two sentinel steps prove the
# gate itself still bites (a scanner that exits 0 from a syntax error must not
# read as green).

on:
  # Every pull request: the gate takes seconds, and a path filter would miss the
  # shared inputs the checker charges (skill includes rendered into SKILL.md,
  # resources read unconditionally, the keep list) — Bridgebuilder F-001 on
  # PR #1266.
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  prompt-budget:
    name: Byte budgets for the prompt surface
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        # actions/checkout@v4.3.1 (pinned per cycle-098 supply-chain pattern)
        uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5

      - name: Check budgets
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          rc=0
          bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --json > prompt-budget.json || rc=$?
          # A checker that dies before writing a report must fail LOUD with its
          # exit code, not as an opaque jq parse error (Bridgebuilder F-003).
          if ! jq -e . prompt-budget.json >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "::error::check-prompt-budget.sh --json produced no parseable report (exit $rc)"
            cat prompt-budget.json || true
            exit 1
          fi
          # Human-readable table for the log; the JSON gate below is the verdict.
          bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh || echo "::notice::human-readable run exited non-zero; the JSON gate decides"
          jq -r '.violations[]? | "::error::prompt budget: \(.)"' prompt-budget.json
          jq -e '.ok' prompt-budget.json >/dev/null

      - name: Positive control (the gate rejects the over-budget sentinel with exit 1)
        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real budget failure above stays the visible failure (Bridgebuilder iter-5 F-003)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          rc=0
          bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --root tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/over --quiet || rc=$?
          if [ "$rc" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "::error::check-prompt-budget.sh did not reject tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/over with exit 1 (got $rc)"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: over-budget sentinel rejected"

      - name: Negative control (the gate accepts the under-budget sentinel)
        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real budget failure above stays the visible failure (Bridgebuilder iter-5 F-003)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if ! bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --root tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/under --quiet; then
            echo "::error::check-prompt-budget.sh false-positive on tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/under"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: under-budget sentinel accepted"

      - name: Upload report
        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real budget failure above stays the visible failure (Bridgebuilder iter-5 F-003)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02
        with:
          name: prompt-budget-report
          path: prompt-budget.json
          retention-days: 14
